editorial:
You step into a quiet suburban house where a young mother has just killed her entire family, and a detective named Muldoon is trying to figure out why. The deeper she digs, the more she realizes the house itself is cursed by a vengeful ghost that latches onto anyone who enters. The vibe is dark, tense, and full of creepy moments that keep you on edge. It is not a fun popcorn scare fest; it is more of a slow, heavy mystery that pulls you into its gloomy world.

The acting is solid, especially from Andrea Riseborough, who carries the emotional weight well. The pacing is steady, though some scenes drag a bit. The scares are effective but familiar if you have seen the older films. Pros include strong atmosphere and a few genuinely unsettling moments. Cons include a confusing timeline and characters you may not care about. If you enjoy supernatural mysteries and do not mind a bleak tone, give it a shot.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Muldoon realizes the curse has already attached to her and her son. She tries to burn the house down to end it, but the ghost follows her home. The twist is that destroying the house does not stop the curse; it simply moves with the people who entered. The movie ends with Muldoon and her son now haunted, showing the grudge spreads endlessly to anyone who comes near it.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves supernatural mysteries and creepy ghost stories.
